title: Complete devissage exists after elementary etale localization
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $S$ generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra, let $N$ be a finite $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime with inverse image $\mathfrak p\subset R$. There exist commutative rings $R_0,S_0$ forming a commutative square $R\to S$, $R\to R_0$, $S\to S_0$, $R_0\to S_0$, and primes $\mathfrak q_0\subset S_0$, $\mathfrak p_0\subset R_0$, such that $\mathfrak q_0$ contracts to $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p_0$, $\mathfrak p_0$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$, the spectrum maps of $R\to R_0$ and $S\to S_0$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and the induced maps $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_0)$ are isomorphisms. The algebra $S_0$ is generated by finitely many elements over $R_0$, and the finite $S_0$-module $N\otimes_S S_0$ admits a complete dévissage over $\mathfrak p_0$ in the sense of [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage]. Residue fields and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No flatness hypothesis is imposed on $N$ or on $R\to S$.

source.place: Tag 05I1, lemma-existence-algebra (forget the extra pointing of the complete devissage at q-prime, retain the complete devissage over p-prime)

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$, and $\mathcal F=\widetilde N$, with the points $b,x$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$. The affine-spectrum dictionary identifies their residue fields with the ring residue fields. The finite generating family of $S/R$ makes $X\to B$ locally finite type by the affine-pairs criterion. The associated sheaf is quasi-coherent, and its global sections are $N$ by the tilde/global-sections isomorphism; the affine finite-type criterion therefore makes $\mathcal F$ finite type. We will construct a pointed affine chain of [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data] after elementary etale changes, then use [lem-trf-pointed-devissage-affine-translation].

The induction is quantified over every locally finite type morphism of affine schemes $X\to B$, every finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$, and every $x\mapsto b$: after elementary etale changes of both pointed schemes there is a pointed affine devissage chain. For the nonzero fibre-stalk case use strong induction on $d=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_b)\geq0$. This integer is finite: the affine-pairs criterion gives a finite generating family for the coordinate algebra, whose images generate its fibre algebra over $\kappa(b)$, and the finite-type dimension theorem makes that fibre finite dimensional. The fibre sheaf is again associated to a finite module: tensor the original finite generating list, and apply the affine finite-type criterion. Its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. Any chain of irreducible closed subsets in this closed support is a chain in the fibre, so its dimension and the minimum defining dimension at a point are finite too. This establishes the induction measure for every auxiliary input, not just the original module.

source.place: Tag 05HR, first proof sentence, with the induction quantified over all affine input data.

proof.text: First handle the zero fibre-stalk case, at any induction stage. On the affine scheme write $\mathcal F=\widetilde L$ with $L$ finite, using the tilde/global-sections and finite-type criteria. The affine pullback and stalk formulae identify $(\mathcal F_b)_x$ with $L_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak m_bL_{\mathfrak q}$. The image of $\mathfrak m_b$ lies in the maximal ideal of the local ring at $x$. Nakayama gives $L_{\mathfrak q}=0$. The finite-type surjective-on-stalk lemma applied to $0\to\mathcal F$ gives an open neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F=0$. Take an affine open neighbourhood inside it. Its inclusion is elementary etale, and the zero sheaf has the length-zero chain by definition. The base can be left unchanged. This case needs no induction hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05HR, terminating zero-cokernel case, with Nakayama and the finite-type zero neighbourhood written explicitly.

proof.text: Suppose now the fibre-stalk is nonzero and its support has dimension $d$ at $x$. Apply [lem-trf-elementary-module-devissage]. Its input hypotheses are exactly local finite type, finite-type quasi-coherence, and this nonzero fibre-stalk. It gives affine elementary etale source and base changes, a finite $\pi:Z\to Y$, a finitely presented closed immersion $i:Z\to X$, $i_*\mathcal G\cong\mathcal F$, the singleton marked fibre, the purely transcendental residue extension, and smooth geometrically integral fibres of relative dimension $d$. Integral after all field extensions implies irreducible after all field extensions, by the definitions. Thus these are the one-step data of [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]. Rename the changed data $B,X,\mathcal F,x,b,Z,Y,\mathcal G,z,y$. We retain $d$ from before the change; no unquoted assertion about invariance of support dimension under etale maps is needed.

Apply [lem-trf-devissage-generic-basis-drop] on $Y$ to $\mathcal H=\pi_*\mathcal G$. It is quasi-coherent by the affine-pushforward theorem, since $\pi$ is finite and hence affine. It is finite type: on affine sections $\mathcal G$ is a finite $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$-module; this ring is finite over $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ by finiteness of $\pi$, and products of two finite generating lists generate the restricted module. The affine finite-type criterion applies. Obtain $\alpha:\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}\to\pi_*\mathcal G$ with the required generic-fibre isomorphism and finite-type quasi-coherent cokernel $\mathcal Q$, whose fibre support has dimension $<d$ if nonempty. If $(\mathcal Q_b)_y=0$, Step 3 gives an open neighbourhood of $y$ where $\mathcal Q=0$. Choose a principal open $W$ inside it: write the complementary closed set as $V(I)$ and take $f\in I$ outside the marked prime. Then $D(f)$ contains the marked point and misses $V(I)$. Apply the target-shrinking part of [lem-trf-devissage-pointed-restriction]. The restricted $\alpha$ is surjective, so the first datum alone is a complete chain of length one. In particular this completes the case $d=0$.

If $(\mathcal Q_b)_y\ne0$, its support dimension at $y$ is an integer strictly less than $d$ by Step 5. Apply the strong induction hypothesis to the affine morphism $Y\to B$ and module $\mathcal Q$. Smoothness includes local finite presentation, hence local finite type (its local finite polynomial presentations have finitely many algebra generators). The induction gives a square of elementary pointed etale maps $(Y',y')\to(Y,y)$ and $(B',b')\to(B,b)$ and a pointed chain for the pullback $\mathcal Q'$ on $Y'$. The base ring is allowed to change because the induction hypothesis in Step 2 quantified over all affine data.

source.place: Tag 05HR, third paragraph: apply induction to the cokernel on Y.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-devissage-pointed-etale-refinement] to the first datum and the square from Step 6. Its hypotheses include the singleton marked finite fibre and purely transcendental extension, both supplied in Step 4. It produces $(B'',b'')\to(B',b')$, elementary $(X'',x'')\to(X,x)$, and affine $Y''\subset X_1:=Y'\times_{B'}B''$, with the new one-step datum and $Z''=Z\times_YY''$. Pull back $\alpha$ using the stated finite-pushforward comparison. Its generic residue-field map is still an isomorphism, and its cokernel is the restriction to $Y''$ of the pullback $\mathcal Q_1$ of $\mathcal Q'$ to $X_1$. By the pointed base-change clause of [lem-trf-devissage-pointed-restriction], the chain of Step 6 pulls back to a chain for $\mathcal Q_1/X_1/B''$. The marked point of $X_1$ belongs to $Y''$.

source.place: Tag 05HR, middle proof paragraphs: 05HE refinement and 05HK pointed base change.

proof.text: Make the first datum and the tail fit exactly. Apply the initial-open shrinking clause of [lem-trf-devissage-pointed-restriction] to the chain on $X_1$ and its open neighbourhood $Y''$. This gives a principal base restriction $B_1\subset B''$ and a principal open $V\subset X_1$ contained in $Y''$, with a chain for $\mathcal Q_1|_V$. Because $V$ is a principal open of $X_1$ contained in the open $Y''$, it is also the principal open in $Y''$ defined by restriction of the same function. First restrict the first datum to $B_1$, then apply its target-shrinking clause to $V$. After a further principal base restriction $B_2\subset B_1$ its smooth target is exactly $V\times_{B_1}B_2$. Base change the shrunken tail to $B_2$, using clause (1) of that same node. Its initial module is now exactly the cokernel of the restricted first $\alpha$. Concatenate the first datum with this tail: the connecting module isomorphism is this cokernel identification, every generic-fibre map is an isomorphism, and the last cokernel is zero. These are every clause of the chain definition. This finishes the strong induction.

source.place: Tag 05HR, final proof paragraph: use 05HM on the tail, then 05HA on the first target, then concatenate.

proof.text: Apply the induction just proved to Step 1 and write its final affine source and base as $\operatorname{Spec}S_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$, with marked primes $\mathfrak q_0,\mathfrak p_0$. Their maps to the original affine schemes give the required commutative ring square, all three contractions, and both residue-field isomorphisms by the affine-spectrum dictionary and the construction. Elementary etale maps compose: their scheme maps are etale by composition, and their induced field maps are composites of isomorphisms. The pullback comparison identifies the final module with $\widetilde{S_0\otimes_SN}$; tensor symmetry $s_0\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes s_0$, with itself as inverse, identifies it with $\widetilde{N\otimes_SS_0}$.

source.place: Tag 05I1, elementary etale square, via the complete induction of 05HR; 05HW elementary-etale-localization definition.

proof.text: Check the algebra hypotheses before the final translation. Put $C=S\otimes_RR_0$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale by base change, and the composite of $\operatorname{Spec}S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ with this projection is the constructed etale source map. Etale cancellation makes $\operatorname{Spec}S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ etale, hence locally finitely presented, and the affine finite-presentation criterion gives finitely many generators of $S_0$ over $C$. The images $s_j\otimes1$ of the original generators of $S/R$ generate $C/R_0$; adjoining the new generators gives a finite generating family of $S_0/R_0$. If $n_j$ generate $N/S$, then $n_j\otimes1$ generate $N\otimes_SS_0/S_0$: write each $n$ as $\sum s_jn_j$ in a pure tensor. Finally apply [lem-trf-pointed-devissage-affine-translation] to the constructed chain, forgetting its marked intermediate points. It gives exactly the complete algebra devissage required by the item. No flatness was used in any step.

source.place: Tag 05I1 and 05I0 (remark-same-notion), first implication; finite type over the changed base checked explicitly.
